payload.keyword_notes: Volumes: only 'legal wedding in bali' returned data (10 a month, AU). 'getting married in bali' is reserved for a future legal spoke: mention once, no exact-match anchor. Never use 'bali wedding packages' or 'bali wedding cost' as anchors.

audience.notes: Australian couples in their 30s, AUD 150K+, multi-day wedding for 60 to 150 guests. Many are of different faiths or none, or have family who care about the ceremony. The paying parent wants to know the marriage will be recognised at home. Top fears: (A) a legal problem surfaces after deposits are paid; (B) running paperwork and suppliers from Australia with nobody accountable.

payload.search_intent: Informational: understand whether Indonesian law requires a religion to marry in Bali, what that means for us, and what to do instead.
payload.angle: State the rule exactly as the Australian Embassy and Law No. 1 of 1974 do, list recognised religions only from an official source, summarise what official texts say for couples of different faiths or no faith without opinion, then show the practical route: marry legally in Australia, celebrate in Bali, with a Wedded Advisor handling the week.
serp_gaps_to_win: No top 3 result in Sydney or Brisbane is written for an Australian couple; win with a plain-English answer in the first 60 words.
No ranking page quotes the Australian Embassy wording or links the official law text.
Interfaith and no-religion content is academic or a law-firm blog; give a neutral, dated summary of official texts only.
Travel-site snippets carry an outdated minimum age; give the current official rule with source and date (researcher to confirm Law No. 16 of 2019).
PAA: 'Is a wedding in Bali legal in Australia?' and 'Is religion required for marriage?' answered cleanly.
payload.word_count_note: Top 3 word counts unknown (snippets only). Template range 1,900 to 2,500; brief for about 2,100 and do not repeat body content in the FAQ.

outline.h2: The Bali marriage religion requirement, in plain words
outline.answers: Does Indonesian law require a religion to marry in Bali?
must_include: Direct answer with the primary keyword in the first 60 words.
The rule as the Australian Embassy in Indonesia states it, citing Law No. 1 of 1974 (same religion, or one partner converts). Where the Embassy mentions conversion, quote it exactly and add nothing.
Link to the official law text (Indonesian government legal database) and the Embassy page.
One line: an Australian celebrant cannot legally marry you in Bali (sourced, as in the packages article).
Key takeaways block after the intro (3 to 4 bullets).

outline.h2: Which religions are recognised for marriage
outline.answers: Which faiths can a legal marriage in Indonesia be conducted under?
must_include: Official list only (Indonesian government source, Embassy or Civil Registry as cited). If no official list is readable, write [[NEEDS: research answer]]; never use a travel site or social post.
Neutral listing in alphabetical order; no description or comment on any faith.
What proof of religion the authority may ask for, only if sourced; otherwise move to the questions list.

outline.h2: Couples of different faiths, or no religious faith
outline.answers: What does the law say if we do not share a religion, or have none?
must_include: Only what official texts state: Law No. 1 of 1974, Constitutional Court rulings on the article (cite case number and date if readable), Supreme Court circular SEMA No. 2 of 2023 (cite exact wording if readable).
No advice to convert; no comment on any faith; no interpretation beyond the text.
If the texts are not readable, say the Civil Registry Office or Indonesian Embassy decides and send the reader there.
Advise not to pay venue deposits until the deciding authority answers in writing (carried rule).

outline.h2: How the legal ceremony and registration work
outline.answers: Who marries us and who registers it?
must_include: Muslim marriages: Office of Religious Affairs (KUA). Other recognised religions: ceremony by a minister of religion, then registration with the Civil Registry Office (Kantor Catatan Sipil / Dukcapil), as sourced.
Notice to the Civil Registry Office 10 days before (as sourced), varies by province.
CNI from the Australian Consulate-General in Bali; Civil Registry Offices do not normally accept a CNI older than three months (Embassy).
DFAT cannot advise on Indonesian requirements.
Invisible work line: documents, translations, timing the CNI, appointment logistics while guests arrive.
Do NOT repeat the packages article's two-routes table; one short paragraph and link up (conditional).

outline.answers: Can same-sex couples marry legally in Bali?
must_include: One factual, sourced sentence (Smartraveller Indonesia or Embassy).
Link to /expert-advice/where-can-same-sex-couples-legally-marry-abroad.

outline.h2: The alternative: marry in Australia, celebrate in Bali
outline.answers: How do we avoid the religion requirement and still have the Bali wedding?
must_include: Marry legally before an authorised celebrant in Australia; the Bali ceremony is symbolic with no legal effect.
NOIM at least one month and no more than 18 months before (AGD), legal ceremony a few weeks before flying; the Bali week holds no legal step (carried rule).
Say plainly how much Indonesian paperwork this avoids (no CNI, no Civil Registry, no religion requirement for the legal marriage).
Recognition: Smartraveller wording, 'usually recognised'; link overseas-marriage-certificate for couples who do marry in Indonesia.
Mid-article soft CTA here.
Link the Bali hub with a descriptive anchor and the villa spoke (conditional).

outline.h2: Questions to ask before you commit
outline.answers: What should we ask the Civil Registry Office, the Consulate-General and our planner?
must_include: 8 to 10 numbered questions, grouped: Civil Registry Office or Indonesian Embassy/Consulate in Australia; Australian Consulate-General in Bali; your planner.
Do not repeat the 4 registry questions already in the packages article verbatim; reword or extend.
Requirements are confirmed by the authority, never by the Wedded Advisor or concierge.

outline.answers: Five quick answers not in the body
must_include: 5 questions, 40 to 60 words each, FAQPage schema, each adds a fact not in the body.

Candidates: Is a wedding in Bali legal in Australia? (PAA; reword so it does not duplicate the packages FAQ); Is religion required for a civil marriage in Indonesia? (PAA); What is the minimum age to marry in Indonesia? (official source only); Can we have a Balinese blessing without it being a legal marriage?; Do we need a translator at the Civil Registry Office? (only if sourced).
Fear A: a legal problem after deposits; tell readers to get written confirmation from the deciding authority before paying venue deposits.
Fear B: who handles the paperwork and suppliers; show what a Wedded Advisor coordinates (timeline, suppliers, guest logistics, the symbolic ceremony) while legal answers come from the authorities.
Rule quoted as the Embassy words it, with Law No. 1 of 1974 named.
Recognised religions from an official list only.
Interfaith and no-religion content from official texts only, dated.
One sentence for same-sex couples with link.
One comparison sentence with a country we cover, if it helps (e.g. a country open to civil marriage for non-residents), from weddings-abroad page.
Key takeaways after intro; mid-article soft CTA; closing discovery_call CTA.
'Sources current as at November 2026' line.
Disclosure line on how Wedded Wonderland is paid, as in the sibling articles, if the concierge section mentions partners.
must_avoid: Any advice or suggestion to convert; any comment, description or value judgement on any faith.
Interpreting the law beyond official texts; academic papers, law-firm blogs, travel sites, Instagram or Facebook as sources.
Research-method language ('search snippets', 'we could not read').
Repeating the packages article's routes table, registry questions or FAQs; repeating cost figures (link the cost guide only if needed).
Promises about approvals, dates or recognition outcomes.
Brand facts from site/ drafts; concierge prices or named contacts (CONCIERGE-PAY open).
Wedded World links; the licence pillar /expert-advice/marriage-licence-requirements (DRAFT).
Em dashes; 'easy', 'simple', 'stress-free', 'most couples', 'dream wedding', 'fairytale', 'tie the knot', 'seamless', 'magical', 'stunning'.
Exact-match anchors for keywords other pages own ('bali wedding packages', 'bali wedding cost', 'getting married in bali').
